scope: Theorem 1.2 of the manuscript “Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields” (preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 142 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ed88aa5ba802311a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a uniform deterministic algorithm with the following guarantee. Its input is a prime p and a nonzero dense polynomial f ∈ Fp[x]. If p > B200000 and n ≥ 2, its input also includes one auxiliary prime ℓq satisfying (1.2) for each prime q ≤ n. It outputs the complete factorization of f, including multiplicities. Let E = max(2, maxq ℓq), with E = 2 when no auxiliary primes are required. For an absolute constant C, the algorithm uses O((B + E)C) bit operations. It uses neither randomness nor an integer factorization or primitive-root oracle.
